tiles.heading: Look here first
tiles.details: CANYON MUHLY ×involuta is an accepted CENTRAL-TEXAS natural hybrid M. lindheimeri × M. reverchonii. NOW actual source-labelled live botanical photographs are LOCATED at UT Austin PlantPics (Bob Harms): habit (MUIN-a), open head with ruler (MUIN-I), and collar/ligule with ruler (MUIN-L). This eliminates the assumption that no real photograph exists, but the UT use terms and whole-site photo count still must be checked before rehosting. The canonical gallery remains a historical multi-taxon plate plus parent photos until import is legal. For reliable ID: fresh FIRM DECURRENT brown-based ligule, tightly folded blades, 3–4 mm spikelets, ~2–2.5 mm glumes and 0.5–2 mm awn. Verify specimen/hybrid origin; intermediate bunch size alone is NOT proof.

tiles.heading: Look-alike comparison
tiles.details: Lindheimer generally makes a larger, coarser more erect bunch with comparatively contracted dense flowering branches; seep muhly makes a smaller fine tuft with an airy delicate head. This natural hybrid may be intermediate and is particularly risky to force from habit-only photos. Ornamental pink-flowered M. capillaris is not a substitute ID.
